findings.issue: The three must_follow edges identify their parent artifacts in prose, but none records the required execution triggers. The phase says c-1 must finish before c-2/c-3 and their amendments are reviewed before work begins, which leaves a QA-wait interpretation and provides no merge-forward protocol for parent development pushes or child fix rounds. c-4 similarly names only the parent sprint. A downstream orchestrator cannot determine when to ingest pushed contract/source changes or whether child completion may precede parent PR merge.
findings.required_correction: For c-2/c-3 consuming c-1 and c-4 consuming c-3, state: parent development push triggers parent-to-child merge-forward before each development/fix round; parent QA is not a start barrier; parent PR merge precedes child PR completion. Preserve named contract artifacts and current three-edge graph. Replace ambiguous finish/review-before-begin language with those explicit triggers; no new sprint or process artifact is needed.

findings.issue: The newly approved configuration-derived boundary policy explicitly consumes ADR-RUN-0303's generated application crate graph in c-1 and requires c-2 to emit and verify its selected crates/edges, but neither sprint lists ADR-RUN-0303 in its authoritative adrs frontmatter. The direct-consumption architecture checklist therefore omits the contract that determines whether the fresh-install policy is correct. The phase ADR index also omits that newly governing decision.
findings.required_correction: Add ADR-RUN-0303 to c-1, c-2, and the phase ADR lists; verify other newly introduced policy references against the requirements/ADR registers and include only the decisions that actually govern the mapping. Retain ADR-RUN-0303 as the graph authority rather than introducing a second graph definition.
